questions.prompt: Which US president oversaw the Louisiana Purchase?
questions.fact: He doubted he had the constitutional authority to do it, and went ahead on the grounds that the opportunity would vanish.

questions.prompt: Which element has the highest melting point?
questions.fact: It melts above 3,400 degrees Celsius, which is why it was used for light bulb filaments for a century.

questions.prompt: How many events are in an Olympic triathlon?
questions.fact: Transitions between them are timed as part of the race, and races have been decided inside them.

questions.prompt: Which television series is set in Albuquerque, New Mexico?
questions.fact: It was written for Riverside, California, and moved for tax reasons, after which the setting became central.

questions.prompt: Which country is home to the Atlas Mountains' highest peak?
questions.fact: The range shields the country's north from the Sahara, which is why its coastal strip is so fertile.

questions.prompt: Who created the character Hercule Poirot's friend Captain Hastings?
questions.fact: She grew so tired of Poirot she called him insufferable, and kept writing him for fifty years anyway.

questions.prompt: What is the term for a company's move to newer systems from legacy ones?
questions.fact: Some banking systems still run code written in the 1960s, because migrating it is riskier than maintaining it.
